articles.name: How can I add a hyperlink or image to my signature?
articles.title: How can I add a hyperlink or image to my signature?
articles.body:
Question

How do I customize my signature with hyperlinks and images? Can I use a locally saved image in my signature?

Answer

No. You can't use an image saved locally on your computer in your agent signature.

To use an image in your signature, upload the file to a public image hosting site or save it as an asset in your knowledge base. This process generates a public URL that you can use in the Markdown code for your signature.

You can use Markdown formatting to add images and hyperlinks to your signature.

To add a hyperlink in Support:

  1. Click your avatar at the top right corner and then select Manage profile. 

  2. Under Signature on the left-hand panel, type the Markdown text below.

    [Link display text]
(https://www.zendesk.com)


Alternatively, add an image that is also a link using this Markdown:

[![alttext](imageurl)](linkurl)
  • Replace linkurl with the link for the image to direct toward
  • Replace imageurl with the link to the hosted image. After you resize the image, use an image host such as imgur.com > Wait five seconds for the image to load > Right-click the image > Select Copy image link. This returns the link to paste instead of imageurl

To display the image without a clickable link, use this Markdown:

![](imageurl)

This functionality also applies to global and brand signatures.

Tip: Use a PNG or JPEG file and size the image to a smaller size, between 5 KB to 50 KB. For optimal display, start with an image size of approximately 120px wide by 40px high. Adjust as needed to maintain the logo proportions. Ensure the image is on an HTTPS server and test the signature in email clients and the Agent Workspace to ensure proper display.

articles.name: A conversation displays an automated resolution but it was escalated to an agent
articles.title: A conversation displays an automated resolution but it was escalated to an agent
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

A conversation in an email escalated to an agent, but it shows an automated resolution. An escalation shouldn’t be an automated resolution. What happened?

Resolution steps

From your description of the behavior, the conversation isn’t an email interaction. It’s a messaging conversation, handled by the AI agent.

The AI agent attempted to escalate the conversation to a human agent, but no agents were available to accept the handoff. For this reason, the escalation couldn't complete. Instead, the bot created a ticket for follow-up and then finished the conversation itself.

This explains why you see both elements:

  • Custom resolution: Escalated to agent — because the bot reached the escalation step and attempted the handoff
  • Conversation status: Automated resolution — because no human agent actually joined the live messaging conversation, so it ended with the bot

While labels can look contradictory at first, labels describe two different parts of the same flow. In this case, it appears to be a failed handoff or no-agents-available scenario in messaging, rather than an email case or a successful live escalation to an agent.

articles.name: Can I prioritize the use case resolution with AI agents and emails?
articles.title: Can I prioritize the use case resolution with AI agents and emails?
articles.body:
Question

With a double intent in emails with an AI agent, can we prioritize the order of my use case resolutions?

Answer

No, there isn't a way to prioritize the resolution with more than one or multiple use cases.

  • The AI agent will try to solve as many use cases as your settings allow.
  • In addition, the AI agent will only start the next use case if the customer asks for it.

articles.name: How can I update a the phone number field of a user with AI agents and an API?
articles.title: How can I update a the phone number field of a user with AI agents and an API?
articles.body:
Question

How can I update a user's phone number field? I can't achieve that with update_user.

Answer

The phone number is a field on a customer object. It is not tied to user identity. You can update this with the Update User API endpoint, which is a custom API call from your AI agent with Integration or action flow.

If you want to change the phone number in the user's profile, you can also use this method to update the user's phone number.

articles.name: Setting up Contact Center on a customer-managed AWS account
articles.title: Setting up Contact Center on a customer-managed AWS account
articles.body:
Use this guide when setting up Zendesk Contact Center on an AWS account that you provide and manage (Bring Your Own Account - BYOA). In this deployment model, you purchase AWS services directly from AWS and are responsible for your AWS account and Amazon Connect environment. Use these steps to provision your AWS environment, configure Amazon Connect and SAML single sign-on (SSO), connect your Zendesk account, and validate the deployment before handoff.

What's my plan?
Add-on Contact Center

Summary: ◀▼

Set up Contact Center on your own AWS account by provisioning the AWS environment, configuring SAML SSO, connecting your account, and validating access before handoff. You’ll also test inbound and outbound calling, recordings, and transcription, then clean up test resources. This setup is for admins managing a BYOA deployment with Amazon Connect, API tokens, Lambda triggers, and telephony validation.

Use this guide when setting up Zendesk Contact Center on an AWS account that you provide and manage (Bring Your Own Account - BYOA). In this deployment model, you purchase AWS services directly from AWS and are responsible for your AWS account and Amazon Connect environment. Use these steps to provision your AWS environment, configure Amazon Connect and SAML single sign-on (SSO), connect your Zendesk account, and validate the deployment before handoff.

Before you begin, make sure you have:

  • Administrator access to the AWS account
  • Administrator access to the Zendesk account and its valid subdomain, such as example.zendesk.com
  • An active Contact Center license

This article contains the following topics:

  • Step 1: Deploy Connect infrastructure stack
  • Step 2: Deploy Contact Center infrastructure stack
  • Step 3: Configure SSO for Amazon Connect
  • Step 4: Configure Connect Access and Validate Settings
  • Step 5: Configure Zendesk Access and Validate Settings
  • Step 6: Activate recordings on AWS
  • Step 7: Test telephony capabilities
  • Step 8: Clean up (Optional)

Related articles:

  • About AWS services in Contact Center
  • Accessing Amazon Connect and AWS Console from Contact Center

Step 1: Deploy Connect infrastructure stack

First, create the Amazon Connect foundation in your AWS account by deploying the Connect infrastructure stack.

To deploy the Connect infrastructure stack

  1. Sign into your AWS account.

  2. Navigate the CloudFormation console and select Create stack > With new resources (standard).

  3. On the next screen:

    • Select Choose an existing template

    • Select Amazon S3 URL

    • Enter: https://zendesk-contact-center-us-east-1.s3.amazonaws.com/connect/cfn.yaml

    • Click Next

  4. On the next screen:

    • Enter a Stack name

    • Enter an InstanceAlias

    • Enter your ZendeskDomain: For example, foo.zendesk.com.

    • Click Next

      Tip: Leave SamlXmlDocument blank.

  5. On the next screen check the three required acknowledgements, then click Next.

  6. Review the stack configuration and click Submit to create the stack.

Step 2: Deploy Contact Center infrastructure stack

Next, deploy the Contact Center components that connect your Amazon Connect instance to Zendesk.

To deploy the core Contact Center infrastructure stack

  1. Request the CloudFormation template to deploy the Contact Center core solution from Zendesk partner support along with Amazon Connect Customer instance ARN.

  2. Zendesk will generate a new CloudFormation template based on the Connect instance ARN and provide a link for it. Assuming you are already logged into your AWS account, simply click on the link.

Note: Zendesk will also provide the metadata.xml file required to configure SAML/SSO in Step 3.

  1. You should be taken directly to the CloudFormation console where you can review the stack parameters.

  2. Acknowledge the access capability disclaimers and click Next.

  3. Review the stack configuration and click Submit to create the stack.

  4. Once the Contact Center core infrastructure stack has been deployed, inform Zendesk partner support so they can activate it.

Step 3: Configure SSO for Amazon Connect

Contact Center users access Amazon Connect services through Zendesk. In this guide, you can use any identity provider (IdP) supported by Zendesk for users to sign in to Zendesk, and Zendesk then brokers their access to your Amazon Connect environment. For an overview of the Zendesk-mediated federation flow, see Understanding single sign-on for Contact Center. For Zendesk sign-in options, see Giving users different ways to sign into Zendesk and Enabling SAML single sign-on. The AWS steps in this step configure the Zendesk-mediated federation from Zendesk to Amazon Connect. For more information about accessing Amazon Connect and the AWS Management Console from Contact Center, see Accessing Amazon Connect and AWS Console from Contact Center.

3.1 Create identity provider for Connect

Create the AWS IAM identity provider that trusts the SAML metadata supplied by Zendesk. This is separate from your corporate IdP, which is configured for Zendesk sign-in.

To create the identity provider for Connect

  1. From the AWS Console navigate to IAM.

  2. Select Identity Providers on the left (under Access Management) and then click Add Provider.

  3. Ensure that the Provider type is set to SAML and then enter a name for the provider. It is recommended to use a name such as ${connect-alias}-idp.

  4. Then, under Metatadata document click the Choose file button and upload the XML metadata file provided by Zendesk.

  5. Click Add Provider

3.2 Create the SSO federation IAM policy for Connect

Define the permissions that Zendesk-federated users need when they access the Amazon Connect instance.

To create the SSO federation IAM policy for Connect

  1. Select Policies under IAM Access Management, then click Create Policy.

  2. Switch to the JSON view and enter the JSON content below.

    Be sure to replace the [AMAZONCONNECTARN] placeholder (including the square brackets) with your Connect instance’s ARN before saving the policy

    {
    "Version": "2012-10-17",
    "Statement": [
        {
            "Sid": "Statement1",
            "Effect": "Allow",
            "Action": "connect:GetFederationToken",
            "Resource": [
                "[AMAZONCONNECTARN]/user/${aws:userid}"
            ]
        }
    ]
}

  3. Click Next.

  4. Enter a policy name such as ${connect-alias}-sso-federation-policy.

  5. Click Create policy.

3.3 Create SSO federation IAM role for Connect

Create the IAM role that Amazon Connect uses to authorize access from Zendesk's federation flow.

To create SSO federation IAM role for Connect

  1. Select Roles under IAM Access Management, then click Create Role.

  2. Select SAML 2.0 federation for the role type.

  3. Select the Identity Provider created in Step 3.1 as the SAML 2.0-base provider.

  4. Ensure Allow programmatic and AWS Management Console access is selected with a non-regional endpoint, then click Next.

  5. On the next page, add the policy created in step 3.2.

  6. Enter a name for the role. For example, ${connect-alias}-sso-connect.

3.4 Information required by Zendesk

Send the federation values to Zendesk so Zendesk can finish connecting your Amazon Connect instance to Contact Center.

Provide the following information to Zendesk to complete the SSO setup:

  • The SAML Aud from the role created in 3.3 , which can found in the role’s trust policy

  • The ARN of the role created in 3.3

  • The ARN of the identity provider created in 3.1

  • The Connect Instance Relay State URL based on the following format:

https://[REGION].console.aws.amazon.com/connect/federate/[CONNECT_INSTANCE_ID]

Note: Replace the [REGION] and [CONNECT_INSTANCE_ID] with the appropriate values.

  • The SAML Login URL as [ZENDESK_INSTANCE_URL]/access/saml/idp/connect

Note: Replace the [ZENDESK_INSTANCE_URL] placeholder with your Zendesk subdomain. For example: https://mydomain.zendesk.com/access/saml/idp/connect.

Step 4: Configure Connect Access and Validate Settings

In this step, you'll validate approved origins, configure a test user, claim a test phone number, and optionally enable outbound dialing in your Amazon Connect instance.

4.1 Validate Approved Origins

Confirm that the Zendesk and Contact Center domains are allowed to communicate with the Amazon Connect instance.

To validate approved origins

  1. Navigate to AWS Management Console > Amazon Connect, then select your instance alias.
  2. Click Approved Origins, then validate that the following 3 domains are present. If any are missing, add them manually:
    • example.zendesk.com
    • https://1162892.apps.zdusercontent.com
    • https://1162894.apps.zdusercontent.com

4.2 Configure test user

Create a test Amazon Connect user whose login matches the corresponding Zendesk user. This lets you verify the federated access flow before testing calls.

To configure a test user

  1. Navigate to the Overview page and click the Log in for emergency access link:

  2. From the Connect Dashboard, navigate to the User Management and click Add new users.

  3. From the Add user page:

    • Enter the First name

    • Enter the Last name

    • Enter the Login (this must match the corresponding Zendesk user’s primary email address exactly, which is case-sensitive)

    • Select the Security profile permissions (Admin, Agent, etc.)

    • Select a Routing profile (Basic Routing Profile)

    • Click Save

4.3 Claim Test Phone Number

Claim a temporary number and route it to the sample inbound flow so you can test telephony.

To claim a test phone number

  1. Navigate to the Phone numbers page and click on Claim a number as shown here:

  2. On the Claim Phone number page:

    • Select Voice as the channel if it isn’t already selected by default

    • Click on the DID tab (Toll free is fine, but DIDs are cheaper for testing purposes)

    • Select the country

    • Select an available phone number from the list

    • Select the “Sample inbound flow (first contact experience)” contact flow supplied by Amazon Connect

    • Click on Save

4.4 Enable Outbound Dialing (Optional)

If outbound calling is part of your validation plan, assign the test number as the caller ID for the basic queue.

To enable outbound dialing

  1. To test outbound calling capabilities, navigate to the Queues page and click on BasicQueue.

  2. On the Edit BasicQueue page, scroll down to the Settings - optional.

  3. Search for and select the phone number you claimed in the 4.3 and click Save.

Step 5: Configure Zendesk Access and Validate Settings

In this step, you'll test SSO, generate and apply a Zendesk API token, and configure call recordings.

5.1 Test SSO Login

Verify that a Zendesk user can sign in with your chosen Zendesk authentication method and then open Contact Center. The authentication method is configured in Zendesk; Contact Center uses Zendesk's federation flow to provide access to the connected AWS services.

For more information, see Understanding single sign-on for Contact Center.

To test SSO login

  1. Log into the target Zendesk account.

  2. Once logged in, allow access to camera, microphone and sound if/when prompted.

Note: Also, ensure that the browser’s pop-up blocker is disabled for the Zendesk subdomain.

  1. Click on the phone icon on the top-right

Note: Zendesk should automatically log you into Amazon Connect. Otherwise, clicking on the phone icon should initiate the SSO login.

5.2 Generate API Token

Create a Zendesk API token for the Contact Center integration to use when connecting your Amazon Connect environment to Zendesk.

To generate an API token

  1. From the Zendesk Support page, click on the Support dropdown menu on the top-left and select Admin center.

  2. Form Admin center, click on the Apps and Integrations icon, select API tokens and click on Add API token.

  3. Copy the newly generated token and save it for the next procedure:

5.3 Apply API token and configure recordings

Apply the token in Contact Center and choose the recording and transcription settings needed for testing.

To apply API tokens and configure recordings

  1. From the Zendesk Support page, click on the Support dropdown menu on the top-left and select Contact center.

  2. From the Overview page, scroll down to the Zendesk Connection area, select your user from the dropdown and paste the API token created in Step 5.2 under API key.

  3. Click Save.

  4. From the Contact center page, click on Tickets, select Unredacted call recording and Unredacted call transcript.

    Note: These settings can be changed later by you or your partner as needed. We choose unredacted recordings and transcripts here strictly for testing purposes.
    Important: You may need to edit the Sample inbound flow (first contact experience) contact flow to ensure the Set recording, analytics, and processing behavior block is configured accordingly as shown below. Note that you’ll need to configure the appropriate redaction parameters on this block and ensure Contact Lens is enabled on your Connect instance to test redaction.

  5. Click Save.

Step 6: Activate recordings on AWS

In this step, you'll validate the recording settings and enable the AWS Lambda triggers that process recordings and transcripts.

6.1 Validate Recording Settings

Check the AWS configuration created for Contact Center and confirm that it matches the recording settings selected in Step 5.3.

To validate the recording settings

  1. From the AWS Console, navigate to the Secrets Manager, locate the secret created by the Contact Center deployment in Step 2 and click on it.

  2. From the Secret details page, scroll down to the Secret value area and click on the Retrieve secret value button to display the Secret’s value.

  3. If the API token was applied correctly in Step 5.3, you should see a token value similar to this one:

  4. Click Close.

  5. Navigate to Systems Manager Parameter Store and locate the following parameters.

    1. zendesk-voice-save-recording

    2. zendesk-voice-save-transcript

  6. Click on each of the parameters and verify that the value is “unredacted” as configured in Step 5.3.

6.2 Enable Lambda Triggers

Enable the event triggers that move recording and transcription data through the Contact Center processing flow.

To enable the Lambda triggers

  1. Navigate to the Lambda console in AWS and locate the following Functions:

    • RecordingIngestLambda

    • ContactLensEventsLambda

    • CTRIngestLambda

    • ZendeskVoicePostCall

    • TranscriptIngestLambda

  2. Click on each of the functions listed above and enable its Kinesis and/or EventBridge triggers:

    1. For EventBridge triggers:

      1. Click on the Configuration tab

      2. Click on Triggers from the menu on the left

      3. Click on the EventBridge trigger link

      4. From the EventBridge Rule details page click on the Enable button at the top.

      5. Navigate back to the function details page and refresh the trigger panel to verify the EventBridge trigger has been enabled.

    2. For Kinesis triggers:

      1. Click on the checkbox next to the Kinesis trigger

      2. Click on the Edit button

      3. From the Edit trigger page, click on the Activate trigger checkbox to enable the trigger and then click Save.

      4. Verify that the trigger was enabled.

Step 7: Test telephony capabilities

In this step, you'll verify federated access, then test inbound and outbound calling.

7.1 Test federated access to Amazon Connect & AWS

Confirm that the Zendesk login services provide the required access to the Amazon Connect Dashboard and AWS Management Console when using the Zendesk-mediated federation configured in Step 3. If you also configured direct federation from your corporate IdP to AWS, test that additional access path according to your AWS identity configuration.

To test federated access to Amazon Connect and AWS

  1. Log out of the AWS Console unless logged into it from an incognito browser tab.

  2. Log out of and back into your Zendesk account.

  3. Navigate to the Contact center configuration console.

  4. From the Overview page:

    1. Click on the Amazon Connect Dashboard link to further validate federated access to the Connect Dashboard.

    2. Click on the AWS Console link to verify access to the AWS Console.

For example:

7.2 Test inbound calling

Test the complete inbound path from the temporary phone number through Amazon Connect, the agent workspace, and the Zendesk ticket.

To test inbound calling

  1. From the Support page in Zendesk, click on the user icon on the top-right corner and select Online to change the agent status to available.

  2. Place a call to the phone number claimed in Step 4.3. Follow the menu options offered by Amazon Connect to be placed in queue and transferred to an agent.

  3. Accept the incoming call, and close the notification presented as shown here:

  4. Speak a few words to validate the recording and call transcription once, then end the call.

  5. Click the Finish wrap-up button to close the Amazon Connect contact .

  6. Wait a few minutes to verify that the call recording and transcription are appended to the ticket as shown below (this may take up to 4-5 minutes):

7.3 Test outbound calling

Test the outbound calling workflow from the Contact Center agent workspace and confirm that the call can be completed successfully.

To test outbound calling

  1. From the Support page in Zendesk, click on the phone icon. Enter a phone number and click Call to dial an outbound call as shown here:

  2. Once the call is connected and your phone rings, click on the End button to hang up.

  3. Click on Finish wrap-up in the pop-up window to close out the contact.

Step 8: Clean up (Optional)

When testing is complete, remove the temporary resources and test data that are no longer needed.

To clean up the test resources

  1. Clear the Outbound caller ID number from the BasicProfile routing profile in Amazon Connect.

  2. Release the phone number claimed in Step 4.3 since it was only intended for testing purposes.

  3. Delete any tickets created in Zendesk as part of testing and validation.

articles.name: Creating, publishing, and managing apps through App Builder
articles.title: Creating, publishing, and managing apps through App Builder
articles.body:
Once you understand the fundamentals of App Builder, you are ready to build, refine, deploy, and maintain your custom applications. This guide walks you through the step-by-step process of using plain language prompts and file uploads to build your app, test its functionality, publish it to your account, and manage versions over time.

What's my plan?
All Suites Professional, Enterprise, or Enterprise Plus
Support Professional or Enterprise

Once you understand the fundamentals of App Builder, you are ready to build, refine, deploy, and maintain your custom applications. This guide walks you through the step-by-step process of using plain language prompts and file uploads to build your app, test its functionality, publish it to your account, and manage versions over time.

Note: App Builder uses artificial intelligence to generate code and configurations based on your inputs. Always thoroughly test apps in a safe environment before deploying them to production.
This is the second article in a series on using App Builder:
  • Using App Builder
  • Creating, publishing, and managing apps with App Builder
  • App Builder code structure reference
  • Troubleshooting App Builder

This article includes the following sections:

  • Creating your first app
  • Designing with file uploads
  • Approving the AI-proposed plan
  • Refining and testing your app
  • Example: Creating an assignee change tracker app
  • Installing and managing apps
  • Integrating with private systems and third-party platforms
  • Next steps
Related articles:
  • Browse all App Builder recipes
  • Create an app recipe: Share your own App Builder creations with the community by submitting a recipe host. See the full instructions to get started.

Creating your first app

To create an app:

  • In Admin Center, click Apps and integrations in the sidebar, then select Apps > App builder. You must be a Zendesk admin to use App Builder.

If you haven't created an app yet, opening App Builder takes you to a welcome page. Click Start a conversation to begin the app creation process.

Returning users land on a conversation list page for quick access to their existing conversations. Conversations are sorted by most recently updated.

When you describe your app, App Builder's AI planner automatically recommends the best location based on your use case (or you can manually change to a different location by clicking Change location). Each app can be built for only one location at a time. Choose from:
  • Ticket Sidebar: Appears alongside each ticket’s details in Zendesk Support (the default). Select this location for displaying ticket-specific information, actions, or integrations. The ticket sidebar applies to existing and optionally new tickets.
  • New Ticket Sidebar: Visible when an agent is creating a new ticket. This location is good for solutions that assist with ticket creation, templates, data enrichment, or validation.
  • User Sidebar: Appears when viewing user profiles. Ideal for surfacing user-specific data, customer context, or account-level actions.
  • Organization Sidebar: Appears when viewing organization profiles. Select this option for displaying organization-level metrics, company details, or business-wide workflows.
  • Top Navigation: The top bar of the Zendesk interface is always accessible regardless of the ticket or screen. Select this option for global tools like notification hubs or quick actions.
  • Side Navigation: Located at the bottom of Zendesk Support’s left-hand navigation panel, this area is ideal for complex or standalone apps that require additional space such as dashboards or reports.

Once you’ve selected the app location, you’ll enter the conversation window. Use one of the provided example prompts or enter your own app requirements and click Send.

Designing with file uploads

To accelerate the app creation process, you can upload up to five files directly into your App Builder prompts. The following file types are supported: PNG, JPG, TXT, DOCX, PDF, CSV, or JSON. The AI analyzes these files to automatically determine the layout, required input fields, and UI components, saving you from writing lengthy, detailed prompts.

To use file uploads:

  1. In the prompt interface, click the paperclip icon. You can attach up to five files per prompt.

  2. Include a detailed description of the app's use case to guide the AI. Be specific about the app’s purpose, required functionality and workflows, UI parts, users, and constraints, as described in the MAPS framework. For example: "Make an app that looks exactly like the attached screenshot for our employee hiring process. Use case: The app will be used by Agents to create new "child" tickets for SMS and email side conversations from parent tickets. The parent and child tickets will have different ticket requesters. The app will handle email child tickets and (if the recipient has opted in) SMS tickets."

  3. Click Send. The AI will parse both your written instructions and the visual elements of your uploaded files to suggest a comprehensive build.

The AI is capable of identifying complex UI elements from your uploads, such as:

  • Recipient input fields with contact validation.

  • Message text areas for custom content.

  • Status indicators (for example, SMS delivery status).

  • Action buttons for specific workflows like "Create Email Ticket."

Once the AI has processed your files, the AI presents a proposed plan for review.

Approving the AI-proposed plan

After you enter your initial prompt, App Builder’s AI generates and presents a recommended plan for your app. You can review the plan, approve it as is, remove unnecessary elements, or incorporate additional suggested features. This approach offers a quick and flexible way to tailor your app to your exact needs.

On the “Approve the plan” screen, you’ll see a summary of your app’s proposed functionality, along with core and optional features. Check or uncheck the boxes next to each feature according to your preference. You can continue making changes later so don't worry if you're unsure now. Here's an example:

At the bottom of the planning screen, you have two choices:

  • Continue planning: Refine the proposed plan further by adding new requirements or making additional adjustments.
  • Approve plan and build: Confirm your selected features and allow App Builder to generate your app based on the approved plan.

Refining and testing your app

After the AI generates your approved plan, App Builder lets you refine, preview, test, and publish your app directly within your Zendesk account.

  • Preview: Click Preview to view your newly generated app in the Preview tab, which uses mock data for a safe first look at the layout, data flow, and interactive elements. This does not guarantee the app will work as expected once published. You should test your app (see below) with real account data before publishing.

    Use the Code tab to review your app's files, folders, and components. Use the Settings tab to review and update your app’s name and logo.

  • Refine and iterate: Refine and update your app at any time by entering new prompts in the conversation pane. Every change is saved, allowing you to experiment freely and revert to a previous version whenever needed. Every change is automatically versioned.
  • Direct code editing: Switch to the native code editor to fine-tune your app's logic, UI, or configuration manually without waiting on prompt iterations or consuming prompt usage. You can make single or multiple code changes across files at once. Whenever a file is modified, a small dot indicator appears next to the file and its parent folder so you can spot unsaved changes. Once you click Save all changes, your edits update the preview. All code edits remain fully compatible with App Builder's visual preview and AI assist.
  • Restore: Each change is saved automatically as a new version, allowing you to revert to any previous version at any time—whether you're experimenting, fixing an error, or reconsidering your approach.
  • Test: Click Test to run your app in Zendesk Support using real account data. Here you can check if your app displays, reads, and writes data as intended and works in real-world scenarios.
    Note: Any updates or changes made while testing your app are applied to your actual account data.
  • Address issues: If something doesn't work, use the app's readable error messages and logs to identify problems. Paste error details into the prompt for targeted help, or ask App Builder to add debugging output.
  • App settings: Customize your app by entering a custom name and selecting an icon along with a background color from the Garden icon library in the Settings tab.
  • Publish and manage your app: When you're fully satisfied, click Publish to make your app available to Zendesk admins or agents.

Choosing a custom app icon

Custom icons make it easier to identify your app and tailor its appearance to your brand or workflow. You have the option to personalize your app’s icon by selecting from Zendesk’s Garden icon library. For each app location, App Builder ensures your icon displays correctly by generating a PNG version of your SVG icon as needed.

To select a custom app icon:

  1. Click the Settings tab.
  2. Enter a name for your app.

    If you don't enter a name, App Builder will automatically generate a name based on the details from your conversation and the prompts you've given.

  3. Browse through a curated collection of Garden icons and background colors. Click any icon or color combination to preview how it will look for your app.
  4. Once satisfied, click Save.

Your selected name, icon, and color will appear in Zendesk Support once published. If you do not pick a custom icon, the default placeholder icon is used.

These settings are saved in App Builder, so the next time you revisit the same app, the latest name and icon choices appear starting from the version where you made those changes.

Version control

App Builder automatically manages versions of your app as you build and iterate, making it easy to experiment, review changes, and recover previous work.

Each time you generate an update or restore a previous version, App Builder creates a new version and records its timestamp.

When a new version is created, you’ll see the version details in your conversation history. Click Restore to return your app preview and code to any prior state. Restoring always generates a new version, so nothing is lost.

You can also select a prior version using the Generated app pulldown menu from the Preview or Code tab.

Example: Creating an assignee change tracker app

Here is an example of building an app for tracking changes in ticket assignees.

  1. In Admin Center, click Apps and integrations in the sidebar, then select Apps > App builder.
  2. Click Start a conversation.
  3. Select Ticket sidebar and click Select location.
  4. At the prompt, enter the following:

    Mission: This app helps to give a very quick view of assignee changes instead of having to dig through the ticket event history, search for all the assignee change events, and track that way. And this is often a question for folks ‘ok, well, where is the handoff in the chain of custody for these tickets’. Action: Create an app called Assignee Change Tracker that tracks the history of changes on an assignee on a given ticket. Parts: A table should list each time the assignee of a ticket has changed, in order of most recent to least recent. Each row should include the assignee’s name, the date they were assigned, and how long they were assigned to the ticket. Above the table, display the total number of changes in assignment of the ticket. Add a button to refresh the displayed data to reflect the latest changes. Add another button to export data to an excel spreadsheet. Make both buttons small and next to each other. Scope: This app is for only the current ticket.

  5. Use the default plan selections and click Approve plan and build.
  6. Click Send.

    App Builder responds with something similar to this:

  7. Review the preview to see how your app looks and behaves, and check the AI’s response prompt to understand the underlying instructions.
  8. Click the Code tab to view the files containing the generated code and mock data used to populate the preview.
  9. At the prompt, enter the following:

    Add Previous Assignee as the first column in the table to capture the full name of the person whom the ticket was previously assigned to. Also add tooltips to both buttons that display a short description of each button's function when hovered over.

  10. Click Send.

    App Builder responds with something similar to this:

  11. Click Test to test your app using your own Zendesk data.

    While testing, any changes you make will affect your actual account, so carefully review the impact of your actions. Also consider customizing your app’s appearance in the Settings tab. For example, update the app’s color and icon to something relevant to your app’s theme rather than using the default icon. This helps to clearly identify your app.

Your app is now complete and is ready to be published.

Installing and managing apps

To install and manage apps:
  1. When you are satisfied with your app, click Publish in the upper right corner.

    You’ll be prompted to set who can access this app by selecting specific Zendesk roles (such as Admin, Agent, and so forth) and user groups. This allows you to limit access based on role or group. For example, restricting the app to only admins, or select user groups.

  2. Acknowledge the service disclaimer regarding the use of apps created through App Builder.

    After you click Agree and Publish, the installation process begins, and App Builder notifies you when your app has been successfully installed.

  3. Click Manage App to modify permissions or manage the app further, or select Apps > Zendesk Supported Apps.

    For more information, see Managing your installed apps.

Note: Apps cannot be moved automatically between different Zendesk instances within your account. If you want to use an app in another instance, you must manually download the app code and upload it to the new instance.

Integrating with private systems and third-party platforms

App Builder makes it easy to connect your app with private company data sources as well as external, third-party platforms by guiding you step by step through connection setup and authentication.

To integrate with private or external services, you’ll typically need the API endpoint and authentication details. App Builder supports two primary authentication approaches:

  • API key authentication: You provide an API key directly as a credential, which authorizes your app to access the external API. This key acts as proof that you’re allowed to use the API. Using an API key is quick and simple, making it ideal for internal systems or cases where you control the API.
  • OAuth 2.0 authentication: Instead of entering an API key, OAuth 2.0 handles a secure handshake between your app and the external service. This method is more secure as it avoids direct API key handling and enables granular permissions. This method is best suited for third-party services where users need to explicitly grant your app access to their data.

App Builder automatically displays the appropriate authentication settings panel when it's needed, often after investigating requirements for a third-party system through its AI-driven web search. The authentication settings panel appears only when you click Test or Publish.

For more information, see Securing API connections in App Builder.

Using API keys

When you create an API key connection, you must specify an HTTP header name. When the connection is used to make an API call, Zendesk passes the API key as the value for this header.

The exact steps for setting up API key authentication varies depends on your integration. Below is one typical example and visual walkthrough.

  1. For Domain, enter the base URL for your account. For example, "testdomain".
  2. Enter the project key. This is a unique key that identifies the project you want this app to connect to. For example "HR".
  3. Click Continue.
  4. Click Test.
  5. Click Next.
  6. For Allowed Domains, enter the full domain you want to allow for this connection. For example, testdomain.atlassian.net.
  7. Enter the API token. This is the secure credential used to authenticate your connection to the service.
  8. Click Create integration and test app.

Using OAuth 2.0

App Builder supports the secure, industry-standard OAuth 2.0 protocol for connecting to third-party and internal APIs. This means you can safely build apps that access data from external systems or your own APIs, using token-based authentication flows instead of sharing static credentials.

Before creating a connection with the OAuth 2.0 authentication type, you must configure an OAuth client. When configuring the OAuth client, you need the client ID, client secret, authorization URL, token URL, and scopes from the external system's OAuth configuration interface or admin portal. These credentials are generated while registering your client application (such as Zendesk) with the external system. The exact steps vary based on the external service. App Builder will try to provide setup instructions for creating an OAuth client in the external system. However, guidance may not be provided if App Builder does not have the necessary details.

There are two approaches to creating an integration that requires OAuth:

  • Explicitly request OAuth: If you know your integration will require OAuth, you can specify this directly in your prompt to App Builder. For example, “Create an app that allows me to add links from my Google Sheets to Zendesk tickets. It should display a list of available Google Sheets. Use OAuth to connect to Google.” When you include a requirement like “use OAuth”, App Builder guides you step-by-step through connecting your app to the external platform using the correct OAuth flow.

  • Automatic detection of OAuth requirements: You don’t need to be an expert in authentication methods to get started. If you describe the functionality you want, such as “connect to Google”, App Builder will recognize when OAuth is required, even if you don’t mention it in your prompt. The system guides you through any required authorization steps.

When you click Test on a generated app that uses OAuth:

  1. Copy the OAuth client callback URL and save it in a secure location. You’ll need to use it as the redirect URI when creating the OAuth client in your third-party OAuth provider system.
  2. OAuth is automatically selected as the authentication type. This option is disabled and cannot be modified.
  3. Enter allowed domains for the connection. You can't change the allowed domains after you create the connection.
  4. Enter the Client ID. This is a unique identifier assigned to your OAuth client, similar to a username for your client.
  5. Enter the Client Secret. This is a confidential key issued when registering your OAuth client.
  6. Enter the Access Token URL. This is the URL used to receive an access token.
  7. Enter the Authorize URL. This is the URL to grant the application’s access to the account.

    For most of the above fields, App Builder will suggest and prefill values. However, always review and verify that the details are correct.

  8. Enter a space-separate list of default scopes. Scopes are permissions that represent what a client application can access on behalf of the user.
  9. Click Next.
  10. In the Grant Type field, enter your authorization code. The OAuth grant type determines how your app will authenticate.
  11. (optional) Check "Allow offline access" to request refresh tokens and to maintain access while the user is offline.
  12. (optional) Enter the OAuth URL subdomain. Enter the custom subdomain for your OAuth provider if required. Leave blank if not applicable.
  13. Click Connect and select an account.

    App Builder redirects you to the third-party OAuth provider to select your account and authorize access.

  14. Copy the Connection ID. You'll need it to reference this OAuth connection when configuring or making authenticated requests from your app.
  15. Click Continue.

The following video shows an example OAuth flow, including testing the app.

The following video shows an example OAuth flow, including publishing the app.

Guided integration

When connecting to private or third-party services that require authentication (such as an API key or OAuth), App Builder’s AI analyzes your prompts in the conversation to determine the necessary connection details.

App Builder displays the relevant authentication settings and automatically captures any required information it can detect from your instructions.

If additional details are needed, App Builder prompts you for the necessary credentials or configuration, guiding you through the connection setup step by step.

Integrating with private company systems

To connect to private or internal systems:

  • Obtain your API endpoint and information about how to authenticate (such as whether you need an API key or OAuth credentials) from internal docs or your development team.
  • For more complex integrations, gather all required credentials (API keys, OAuth tokens) and define the input and output data formats your app will use.
  • When you’re ready to set up the connection, prompt App Builder with the information you’ve gathered and you’ll be guided through the remaining steps. Note that App Builder is not familiar with your internal systems and can only assist if you provide relevant documentation or details about these systems.

Once your integration is configured, click Test in App Builder to verify integration functionality before deploying to your live Zendesk environment.

Integrating your app with third-party platforms

App Builder lets you create applications that can display or manipulate data to or from any third-party applications, such as Jira, Slack, Google, Calendly, Workday, and others, as long as those services have public-facing APIs. For example, you could build a Google Sheets integration that allows agents to quickly view or update customer records, ticket logs, inventory lists, or workflow trackers without leaving Zendesk. The app could present real-time data from specific spreadsheets or ranges, and even let agents add new entries, update cell values, or archive old records directly from the Zendesk interface. After each action, the app notifies the agent whether it was successful or if there were any issues with the integration.

Next steps

Learn how application files are organized in App Builder code structure reference.

articles.body:
While App Builder handles underlying code generation through natural language, advanced users can inspect and directly modify application files. This reference guide provides a breakdown of the code tab structure, component layout, and file organization used by App Builder applications.

While App Builder handles underlying code generation through natural language, advanced users can inspect and directly modify application files. This reference guide provides a breakdown of the code tab structure, component layout, and file organization used by App Builder applications.

Note: App Builder uses artificial intelligence to generate code and configurations based on your inputs. Always thoroughly test apps in a safe environment before deploying them to production.
This is the third article in a series on using App Builder:
  • Using App Builder
  • Creating, publishing, and managing apps with App Builder
  • App Builder code structure reference
  • Troubleshooting App Builder

This article includes the following sections:

  • Exploring the code tab and app settings
  • Next steps

Exploring the code tab and app settings

After building and refining your app with App Builder, you can access the Code tab to view all code files and folders generated for your app.

File or folder Description
blueprint.md A high-level summary of the app's purpose, architecture, features, integration details, and key technologies used (such as React, Zendesk Garden components, and so forth).
changelog.md A chronological log of all changes and updates made during the app's development. Use this to track progress and roll back if needed using the Generated app pulldown menu or Version in the conversation history.
index.jsx This is the main source file for your app. It manages how the app loads, handles errors, applies themes, and serves as the entry point for the app functionality.
mock.js This file contains the mock data used for previewing the app's appearance and testing UI flows within the App Builder environment.
components This folder contains React components that define your app's interactive user interface and structure.
styles This folder contains stylesheets to ensure a consistent look and feel.
utils This folder contains helper functions and utility code used throughout your app. These functions perform tasks such as formatting dates, filtering data, and so forth.
Familiarity with your app's code structure lets you diagnose and fix issues more efficiently. You can:
  • Track changes over time, using the blueprint and changelog files.
  • Find and fix issues easily, since you'll know where to look if something isn't working.
  • Experiment safely with styles, mock data, or new features.

Even if you don't write code every day, understanding the structure helps you build, refine, and maintain apps confidently.

For more information about the code, see Apps in the Zendesk developer docs.

At the top, you'll find the following:

  • Options menu: Click the three vertical dots to give feedback or download the conversation as a JSON file. Downloading the conversation is especially helpful when troubleshooting as it allows your team to review the full conversation details if a user encounters an error they cannot resolve. You can also access the Prompting Guidelines help center article to view strategies and examples for clearly communicating your needs to App Builder.
  • Generated app: Use the menu to choose and preview different versions of your app. This allows you to review specific versions, compare changes, and restore previous functionality as needed.
  • Test: Click to view and interact with the app in Zendesk Support. Testing your app here lets you explore and assess its functionality using real data from your Zendesk account. Any updates or changes you make while testing the app will be applied to your actual account data. Be sure to verify that the app behaves as intended before deploying it to your team. If you encounter an error while testing, it is not resolved automatically upon publishing. Publishing only makes the app available in your Zendesk account. It does not fix errors. Be sure to resolve any issues during testing to ensure your app works as expected after publishing.
  • Publish: When you’re ready to release your app, click Publish. This installs the app and makes it available for agents to use.

Next steps

Learn how to troubleshoot App Builder using debugging techniques and common solutions.

articles.body:
When building apps with AI assistance, you may occasionally encounter syntax errors, unexpected behaviors, or API integration issues. This article provides common troubleshooting techniques and solutions to resolve errors during the app creation and testing processes.

When building apps with AI assistance, you may occasionally encounter syntax errors, unexpected behaviors, or API integration issues. This article provides common troubleshooting techniques and solutions to resolve errors during the app creation and testing processes.

Note: App Builder uses artificial intelligence to generate code and configurations based on your inputs. Always thoroughly test apps in a safe environment before deploying them to production.
This is the fourth and last article in a series on using App Builder:
  • Using App Builder
  • Creating, publishing, and managing apps with App Builder
  • App Builder code structure reference
  • Troubleshooting App Builder

This article includes the following sections:

  • Troubleshooting
  • Disclaimer and maintenance

Troubleshooting

App Builder may encounter errors that require additional context or information to resolve. Some examples of these errors include:

  • The preview cannot be loaded.
  • The app cannot be generated or installed.
  • Integration with a private company system or third-party platform fails.

When App Builder encounters issues, it will attempt to resolve them automatically. If it cannot, it will present you with an error message. Click Show error details to view more information about the problem.

To help App Builder diagnose and fix the issue, provide clear and specific details in your conversation. This may include clarifications, credentials, or any missing context related to the error. The AI uses this information to better understand the problem and either resolve it or ask for more details.

For example, if the expected output was a specific data format or a particular response from the app, but the actual output was different, detailing these discrepancies will enable App Builder to troubleshoot effectively and suggest appropriate solutions. The more precise and detailed the feedback, the better the AI can learn from the interaction and improve its responses in future scenarios.

When you test your app with live data in your Zendesk instance, such as fetching or updating records, or integrating with third-party apps, errors may appear that wouldn’t be visible when using mock data in preview mode. Most apps seem to function correctly in the Preview tab unless there’s a code compilation issue that prevents the preview from loading. Guardrail notifications will alert you to any such errors during testing with real data. If you encounter an error, copy the details and paste them into the conversation to help App Builder analyze and resolve the issue.

Here are some common error codes you may encounter:
  • 401: Unauthorized Error - This indicates that the user does not have the necessary permissions to access the requested resource.
  • 403: Forbidden Error - This occurs when a user is logged out of Admin Center after their session expires while App Builder remains open in their browser. It can also arise from integration failures.
  • 404: Not Found Error - This error signifies a broken or incorrect URL, or it may indicate that the requested API path is incorrect or unavailable.
  • 431: Request Header Fields Too Large - This error usually occurs after an extended series of prompts. To resolve it, try clearing the cache and cookies for the Zendesk app in your browser.
  • 503: Service Unavailable Error - This error occurs when the server receives too many requests, causing it to exceed its resource limits. This can also happen if the server is down for maintenance or updates.

Disclaimer and maintenance

Apps created using App Builder are considered non-Zendesk services. You are responsible for verifying that your app functions as intended and for maintaining it over time. Zendesk does not guarantee the functionality, support, or continued maintenance of apps built with App Builder.

articles.name: Announcing endpoint changes for the Ultimate Public API
articles.title: Announcing endpoint changes for the Ultimate Public API
articles.body:
As part of our commitment to improving the stability and performance of our AI services, Zendesk is migrating Ultimate Public API services to the Zendesk Operating System (ZOS). This migration ensures a more unified experience and better integration with your existing Zendesk infrastructure.

This announcement includes the following topics:

  • What is changing?
  • Why is Zendesk making this change?
  • What do I need to do?

What is changing?

Zendesk is updating the endpoints for the Ultimate Public API. Effective immediately, you must update your API endpoints from the legacy Ultimate domain to your dedicated Zendesk subdomain. 

  • Legacy URL structure: *.ultimate.ai
  • New URL structure: <yoursubdomain>.zendesk.com/ai-agents/api

These new endpoints are required for continued use of the Public API following the migration to the Zendesk Operating System.

Note: This change applies to Public API requests. It excludes default automatic webhooks, which Zendesk will migrate automatically. Custom webhooks may still require manual updates. See Webhook migration details below.

For more information, see AI Agents in our developer documentation.

Why is Zendesk making this change?

This update is a key preparation step for our broader platform migration to ZOS. By transitioning to Zendesk-hosted endpoints, we can deliver:

  • Seamless routing: Direct integration within your existing Zendesk infrastructure.
  • Minimal service disruption: Standardized routing through the Zendesk edge network layer.
  • Enhanced scalability and security: Improved overall system performance and protection for your AI agents.

Updating your endpoints ahead of time ensures that your custom integrations remain operational, reliable, and performant once the ZOS migration completes.

What do I need to do?

To avoid service interruptions, you must update your API configurations to point to the new Zendesk endpoints by September 15, 2026. 

  1. Identify all applications, scripts, and webhooks making requests to *.ultimate.ai.
  2. Replace *.ultimate.ai with your account-specific Zendesk URL format: <yoursubdomain>.zendesk.com/ai-agents/
  3. Test your endpoints in a sandbox or non-production environment prior to the deadline.

If these changes are not completed by September 15, 2026, you will be unable to use the Public API post-migration.

Webhook migration details

Zendesk will automatically migrate the default Ultimate automation webhook that was created during your bot setup. No action is required for this default webhook.

In Zendesk, this webhook is typically named Ultimate.ai Automation Webhook: <botId>

The webhook name can be changed, so the name alone may not always identify it. The default webhook is the one associated with the bot configuration created during setup.

Only the default webhook created as part of the bot setup is automatically migrated. Any other customer-created or custom-configured webhooks should be reviewed to ensure they use the appropriate new Zendesk URL structure.

If you have feedback or questions related to this announcement, visit our community forum where we collect and manage customer product feedback. For general assistance with your Zendesk products, contact Zendesk Customer Support.
